channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Taliban voices 'serious concern' over US plan to deport Afghan migrants via Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban government expressed concern on Monday over reported US plans to deport more than 150 Afghans from the US to Pakistan for an eventual return home, with advocacy groups warning the removal could endanger their lives.

item.title: Liga: Yan Diomandé and Kylian Mbappé score again for Real Madrid
item.description: Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomandé have once again scored for Real Madrid against Santander (3-0). After a difficult start to the season, Real Madrid have now won 9 of their last 10 games.

item.title: Live: Russia and Ukraine trade blame for cyber attacks as fragile ceasefire ends
item.description: Russia and Ukraine on Monday traded accusations over cyberattacks, with Moscow reporting a hack of its emergency alerts app hours after Kyiv said its own air raid warning system had been compromised. The incidents came as a fragile ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region expired, raising fears of renewed fighting. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: 9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
item.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy says all nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas.

item.title: Midterms 2026: Georgians on the front lines of the people’s war against data centres
item.description: Artificial intelligence emerged as a major issue on the 2026 US midterm campaign trail, with opposition to data centres drawing supporters across partisan divides united over ecological worries, increased utility bills and business interests outweighing citizen concerns. Georgia, the top US market for data centre construction, has been on the front line of the struggle.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump attacks El-Sayed during stump speech in Iowa
item.description: President Donald Trump visited Iowa and Kansas on Sunday.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of hacking emergency alert apps
item.description: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of hacking their emergency alert applications after a local ceasefire in the war's eastern Kherson region expired on Sunday. The cyberattacks came as both sides warned of renewed fighting and Kyiv signalled it could halt strikes on Russian oil refineries in exchange for US Patriot missiles.

item.title: Halloween weekend shootings across US leave at least six dead, dozens wounded
item.description: A spate of shootings in nightlife districts and near university campuses across the United States over Halloween weekend left at least six people dead and dozens wounded, with Dallas recording the highest toll. Police were investigating multiple incidents in several states, while some suspects remained at large.

item.title: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
item.description: Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed have feuded publicly recently over a campaign ad Stevens said was anti-Semitic.

item.title: WATCH: Runner looks forward to his 50th straight NYC marathon
item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks to 83-year-old Dave Obelkevich ahead of his record 50th straight NYC marathon race and why it’s a tradition for him and his family.

item.title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, chief of staff says
item.description: U.S. Sen. Chris Murphy has been hospitalized after suffering a stroke, his chief of staff said in a statement on Sunday.

item.title: Iran warns renewed war with US could outlast previous conflict
item.description: Iran on Sunday said that a renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, as President Donald Trump suggested that Washington still had targets to strike. Tehran threatened retaliation without geographical limits while diplomatic efforts continued to avert a fresh escalation ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections.

item.title: DOJ urges sanctions for database analysis critical of its noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Justice Department is urging a federal judge to consider whether to hold an immigrant rights group in contempt of court for disclosing the results of its analysis of a dataset of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California

item.title: Nine killed as business jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood
item.description: A business jet plunged into a South Florida neighbourhood on Sunday, killing all nine people aboard and exploding into a fireball near homes and a busy road. The pilot had reported icing, precipitation and severe turbulence before the Learjet entered a steep dive, according to air traffic control recordings.

item.title: French presidential candidate Édouard Philippe rejects centre-right primary
item.description: French presidential candidate and former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe ruled out competing in a primary Sunday, following a proposal made last week by his rival Gabriel Attal to organize a vote to select a single centre-right candidate.

item.title: UN’s peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
item.description: The 35-year-old UN peacekeeping mission ⁠in the disputed Western ​Sahara region came to an end Sunday after the Security Council failed to ​renew its mandate. Morocco, which claims the region as its own, welcomed the decision, while its opponents from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front called it "unacceptable".

item.title: Pilot's last words before jet crashes in Florida, killing all nine on board
item.description: A business jet has crashed in a Florida neighbourhood killing all nine people on board.

item.title: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event today with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.

item.title: Michigan ‘Betrayal’ & Mid Term Manouvres
item.description: France 24’s Spotlight Presenter Gavin Lee assesses the last minute campaign dramas and takes an US election overview on the ‘must watch states’ alongside Professor Donald Green, Professor of Political Science at Columbia University and co-author of the definitive book ‘Get Out the Vote’, and foreign affairs analyst Laurie Dundon, who previously served in the U.S. State Department during the Clinton administration.

item.title: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy is hospitalized with a stroke
item.description: Murphy's office says he was taken to the hospital this weekend after experiencing numbness in his arm. His chief of staff said he is responding well to treatment and expected to make a full recovery.

item.title: How to think about the midterms — and the political moment the country is in
item.description: Polls show Democrats with an advantage in the midterm election but there are potential limitations and results may take a while to roll in.

item.title: Judge tosses Trump's attempt to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
item.description: A federal judge has dismissed a highly unusual lawsuit by the Trump administration that tried to block the certification of results from Alaska's U.S. Senate race if the Republican incumbent lost.

item.title: The midterms will test the nation's political direction and confidence
item.description: At least some portion of the nation is likely to have its political confidence — and perhaps even its sense of security — tested in the days and weeks ahead. That test could also continue for some time to come.

item.title: France: Route du Rhum yacht race sets off
item.description: The 115 sailors competing in the Route du Rhum set sail from Saint-Malo on Sunday in mild weather, embarking on a solo transatlantic crossing. The race began at 12:02 GMT, with boats heading along the Brittany coast in light winds towards a mandatory checkpoint near Cap Fréhel, where crowds had gathered to watch. One competitor, Nicolas d’Estais, described the conditions as ideal before boarding his yacht, Café Joyeux. Selina Sykes reports from Saint-Malo.

item.title: Thousands join Indian opposition protest
item.description: India’s opposition parties staged major protests in New Delhi on Sunday against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and a nationwide voter list review that has fuelled demonstrations since the summer, led by the youth movement Cockroach Janta Party. Eliza Herbert reports.

item.title: Oleshky: Evacuations during first humanitarian truce of war end
item.description: A successful evacuation. Residents of the city of Oleshky who had requested to be evacuated were reunited with their loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31. The city, located on the front line and under Russian occupation, is facing a humanitarian crisis, with civilians lacking even the most basic necessities. A localised ceasefire has been in place since Tuesday. France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze shares the latest.

item.title: New York City Marathon: Sweden's Almgren and Kenya's Chepkirui win as 60,000 take part
item.description: Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race of the New York City Marathon in his debut in the event while Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race on Sunday for the second time.

item.title: France reports largely peaceful protests
item.description: France sees third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, with more than 320,000 people taking to the streets. Most demonstrations remained peaceful, although police used tear gas to disperse clashes. Authorities reported more than 770 arrests nationwide. France24 journalist Jamie Smith-Maillet shares further insights.

item.title: Data centres on the ballot: could the AI infrastructure shape US midterms?
item.description: Voters from Ohio to Illinois decide dozens of local measures on Tuesday, as opposition to the giant buildings powering AI cuts across party lines.

item.title: Oleshky residents return to Ukraine
item.description: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-held territory following a rare local truce. They described years of isolation, food shortages and regular shelling, with some saying they were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive. Seized by Russian forces in the early days of the 2022 invasion, the city remains cut off by the Dnipro River on one side and Russian troops on the other.

item.title: French high school blockades to restart on Monday, student unions say
item.description: The head of a student union said Sunday that high school blockades throughout France would restart on Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron has called for classes to resume after the government announced new measures to address the ongoing education crisis which student groups found insufficient.

item.title: US Midterms: Democrats face leftward surge
item.description: As Democrats seek to regain control of Congress, divisions within the party are emerging over its future direction. A new wave of progressive candidates is pushing to shift priorities further to the left, challenging corporate money in politics and calling for universal healthcare, climate action and an end to police violence. Monte Francis reports.

item.title: Poland rocked by Constitutional showdown
item.description: Poland’s constitutional crisis deepened on Saturday as the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The standoff comes ahead of next year’s parliamentary election, with polls suggesting a close race between Tusk’s coalition and the nationalist right. Camille Corcoran reports.

item.title: France: Route du Rhum fleet ready to depart
item.description: The Route du Rhum, billed as the world’s biggest solo transatlantic race, is set to depart from Saint-Malo in Brittany. Skippers will sail alone to Guadeloupe, with professionals and amateur sailors competing in the race, held every four years. Selina Sykes reports.

item.title: Ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region ends after Russia refuses extension
item.description: The longest truce of the war in Ukraine, localised in the region of Kherson, ended on Sunday after Russia refused to extend the ceasefire. The temporary pause in fighting, which began on Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied town of Olechky.

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.title: The week in pictures: Lula's victory, Israeli elections and Spain train crash
item.description: From Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil's presidential polls, to razor-sharp margins in the Israeli general elections, to a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: A day of celebration in Senegal as the Youth Olympic Games get underway
item.description: It is a historic day for Africa and Senegal. For the first time ever, an Olympic competition is being held on African soil. The Youth Olympic Games officially got underway in Senegal in the Dakar region on Saturday, with an opening ceremony attended by 30,000 people. The competition, which brings together 2,700 athletes aged between 14 and 17, will take place across three Senegalese cities, with 25 sports on the programme.

item.title: Former Ireland European 1,500m champion dies at age of 34
item.description: Former European 1,500m champion Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.

item.title: National Grid sparks deal to pave way for giant UK data centre
item.description: National Grid has struck a deal paving the way for Britain’s biggest electricity substation to be built on Teesside as the government races to avoid missing out on global demand for AI infrastructure development.

item.title: WATCH: The volunteers helping get the NYC marathon running
item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.title: The King to speak about slavery with 'unflinching honesty'
item.description: The King will speak about slavery with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" in a speech to Commonwealth leaders amid increasing pressure for Britain to offer an apology over its role in the transatlantic slave trade.

item.title: UN demands investigation into death of staff member in Houthi custody
item.description: A Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office has died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily held for more ​than two years, the UN human rights chief has said.

item.title: Judge dismisses Trump's Wall Street Journal lawsuit
item.description: A US judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: 1 dead, 6 injured in 'targeted' shooting at California Halloween store
item.description: One person was killed and six others were injured in a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store inside the Solano Town Center in Fairfield, California, police said.

item.title: Judge says court will investigate government officials in DC golf course case
item.description: The judge wants to know if lawyers tried to mislead her over Trump's plans.

item.title: WATCH: Exploring the ancient origins of Halloween
item.description: Travel expert Gabe Saglie talks about Ireland's boost in tourism from Halloween-enthusiasts.

item.title: Majority of funds stolen in cryptocurrency hack replenished, Binance says
item.description: Around 90% of stolen cryptocurrency assets following a hack on a major exchange has been replenished, according to Binance.

item.title: Man dies and another injured after attack at centre housing migrants
item.description: A man has died following an attack at a centre housing migrants in Ireland.

item.title: Texas Democrats see data centers as a winning issue
item.description: Rural Texas voters have overwhelmingly backed Republicans for decades, but Democrats hope voter opposition to data centers could help unseat the Republican governor.

item.title: WATCH: Suspected sailboat thief killed in Rhode Island police shootout
item.description: Body camera footage shows the dramatic police shootout that left a suspected sailboat thief dead in Newport, Rhode Island. The 40-foot boat was stolen back in August.

item.title: Peltola denies knowing of 'any other candidate' on ballot besides herself, incumbent
item.description: The DOJ is acting to "intensely and swiftly" escalate its probe, the top federal prosecutor in Alaska said.

item.title: These House races could determine which party is in control in the next Congress
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are on the ballot when voters head to the polls on Nov. 3.

item.title: DOJ says election officials could face jail time if they fail to preserve records
item.description: The DOJ has warned election officials in multiple states that they could face jail time if they fail to preserve election records in accordance with federal law.

item.title: WATCH: How to keep pets safe on Halloween
item.description: Experts say some candy can contain ingredients that owners may not know are dangerous. Dr. Gary Richter, veterinarian and founder of "Ultimate Pet Nutrition," shares more pet safety tips.

item.title: Voters weigh citizenship amendments as Trump fans fears of noncitizen election fraud
item.description: Civil rights groups warn millions of Americans could get sidelined.

item.title: WATCH: Baby loons play with their moms in must-see video
item.description: You can see more about the baby loons and other animals on "Inside the Enchanted Waterways" on Disney+.

item.title: G20 photocall axed after Miliband and other ministers refuse to be pictured with top Russian diplomat
item.description: A photocall of foreign ministers was cancelled by the US after the UK's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and other European counterparts refused to be pictured with Russia's envoy Sergei Lavrov.

item.title: States push back on Trump's noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Trump administration has warned several states that their voter rolls include noncitizens, but many of those claims haven't held up to scrutiny.

item.title: WATCH: What we know about Binance security breach
item.description: Dave Merkel, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity company Expel, talks about the major breach.

item.title: WATCH: State of the race with 4 days until midterm vote
item.description: Nearly 45 million people have already turned out to vote, and those early voting numbers have surpassed where the numbers were at this point in the 2022 midterm election.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise cancels global trip over rising fuel costs, strands 200 passengers in Cambodia
item.description: Some passengers sold their home to live on the cruise ship full-time.

item.title: WATCH: Remembering Patrick Stewart in his own words
item.description: As tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart, World News Tonight remembers his interview with Diane Sawyer – sharing how theater became his safe space and his home.

item.title: WATCH: See National Geographic's best destinations for 2026
item.description: ABC News' Sam Champion highlights some of the must-visit places featured on National Geographic's annual list of the world's best travel destinations.

item.title: WATCH: NICU babies dressed up for Halloween
item.description: The tiniest patients of the Cleveland Clinic Children's Hospital wear their first-ever Halloween costumes.

item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events
